assign.brief: Owner, on /framework/ux/Dictate/ (2026-10-01): 'I like that the AI transcription works when we click the button and first open it up, it turns the microphone on automatically. But I don't necessarily like that closing it stops recording.' Keep the auto-start-mic-on-open behavior as is. Change: closing the ✦ sheet should NOT stop/release the microphone — dictation should keep running in the background (so the owner can keep talking and see it land once they reopen, or it keeps posting to the conversation). Note the real constraint from ux/Dictate/readme.md's 'Watch out': every live Dictate already stops itself on `visibilitychange`(hidden)/`pagehide` (mic-hijack rule, so another app's mic isn't blocked) and a Dictate taken OFF the page while live also stops itself — closing the sheet may currently be unmounting/removing the Dictate instance from the page, which is what's triggering the stop, not a visibility change. Find the sheet's close handler (ext/drawer/ or wherever the ✦ sheet mounts/unmounts the Widget), find why closing it stops the mic, and change it so the mic keeps running after close (likely: don't unmount the live Dictate on close, just hide the sheet UI) while still respecting the real page-hidden/pagehide mic-hijack rule. Verify, and land per finish-task.

log.msg: root cause found: ext/drawer/rail.js's own hide() explicitly called stop_mic() on EVERY hide (closing the sheet, widening past 52em). The mic-hijack visibilitychange/pagehide rule in Dictate.js was never the cause — the widget stays mounted in the DOM across a hide (CSS class only), so Dictate's own isConnected check never fired.

decision.what: only stop the mic on the breakpoint-widen hide, not on a real close (the ×, drag down, phone back)

The page-hidden/pagehide mic-hijack rule in Dictate.js is untouched.
